method.method_draft: Use the qualitative force rule for parallel currents. First read the diagram: the two long wires are parallel along the drawn +y direction; the pink left wire carries current I along +y, while the blue right wire carries current 2I in the opposite direction, along -y. The blue 2I wire is displaced to the right of the pink wire, i.e. in the +x direction according to the axes shown. From the text, note that the currents are opposite. Apply the rule that parallel wires with currents in opposite directions repel. Therefore the blue 2I wire is pushed away from the pink wire; since it lies to the +x side of the pink wire, the force on wire 2I is in the +x direction.

method.method_draft: Use the magnetic-field direction plus Lorentz force law. From the image, identify the pink I wire as carrying current along +y and the blue 2I wire as carrying current along -y; the blue wire is located at positive x relative to the pink wire. Compute only directions: the magnetic field made by the pink wire at a point to its +x side is given by the right-hand rule around a +y-directed current, so B at the blue wire points in the -z direction. The force on the blue wire is dF = I2 dL x B, with dL for the blue current along -y. Thus (-y) x (-z) = +x. Hence the magnetic force on wire 2I is in the +x direction.
